spec.title: Graph coordinates that explain the plan

status.comment: Owner requires the graph itself to communicate the goal, decomposition and execution order, without relying only on marker selection.

p.planning-navigation: The read model provides explicit references to the active outcome, adopted-plan members and current focus when those facts are available. Object labels and arbitrary array positions are not identity or execution evidence. Goal cards and membership come from registered source data. Current work, proposed starts and historical start are distinct facts; absence of historical or readiness evidence remains explicit.

p.goal-layout: The default goal view anchors the explicitly identified goal and places its milestones and work outward according to their known decomposition and membership. A visible legend explains the meaning of distance and grouping. Resources, sources and other supporting objects retain their meaning without appearing to be mandatory execution stages. These coordinates are a client projection and never become algorithmic priority, effort or duration claims.

p.execution-layout: A work-order view lays out verified prerequisite relations from prerequisite to dependent. Work prerequisites already have this orientation in the ZAP strategic-map contract. Hierarchy, resource use, support and reference relations do not imply execution order. The graph shows direction, dependency stages, entry points and current work or focus directly where supported. Nodes in the same stage have no order established by those dependencies; resource availability and other admission conditions remain separate. Stage labels do not invent a total order or a calendar estimate.

p.partial-and-stability: The projection handles missing goals, incomplete dependencies, off-view prerequisites, disconnected objects and cycles explicitly. It does not make an arbitrary placement look like a verified order. Compute structural placement and entry classification from the full loaded snapshot before applying display filters; filtering cannot invent a new start or reverse the remaining work. Stable source structure keeps stable coordinates across background refresh. Distinct relationships remain inspectable even when their visual treatment is simplified.

p.acceptance: A small explicitly synthetic plan demonstrates a goal, an initial completed task, current work, parallel branches, prerequisites and milestone/resource context. Structural checks cover direction, branching, partial data, cycles and filtering stability. Browser acceptance verifies both coordinate views, visible explanatory labels and legend, selection and navigation, and the owner-selected light/dark palette. A graph should explain its basic structure before the user opens an object card.
